mainTopic: What the seller keeps when he holds back the upper story (עלייה), and what the words 'depth and height' (עומקא ורומא) include when selling a house
overview: The גמרא asks what practical difference comes from ריש לקיש's statement that a seller keeps the upper story (עלייה). רב זביד says the seller may extend projections (זיזין) out over the courtyard. רב פפא says he may rebuild the upper story if it falls. רב זביד's answer fits ריש לקיש's opening words 'זאת אומרת', but רב פפא's does not, and the גמרא ends with קשיא. Next, רב דימי מנהרדעא teaches that a house sale needs two phrases. 'Depth and height' (עומקא ורומא) gives the buyer the space below and above, since a plain sale does not include it. 'From the depths of the earth to the height of the sky' gives him the pit, cistern and tunnels. The גמרא tries to support him from a משנה, but pushes the proof aside by reading that משנה another way. In that reading, a plain sale includes depth and height, and the written words add the pit and cistern. Finally, the גמרא brings another line of the משנה, about a roof with a railing ten טפחים high, to test the question again, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What practical law does the statement teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference comes from ריש לקיש's earlier statement that the seller keeps the upper story.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what practical law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed to say the upper story stays with the seller. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper story was never sold, so of course it still belongs to the seller. The גמרא wants to know what extra right ריש לקיש is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: For what practical law? (What difference does it make?)
Upper story, a room built on top of the house

phrases.english: For what law?
phrases.notes: This refers back to ריש לקיש's earlier statement that the upper story stays with the seller.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference that comes from saying the seller keeps the upper story

steps.title: רב זביד: the seller may extend projections
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that the seller may build projections (זיזין) out from the upper story.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: If the seller wants to put out projections from it, he may do so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives the first answer. The seller may build beams or ledges sticking out from his upper story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping the upper story gives the seller more than just the room. It also lets him use the air space outside it for projections, even though the area below belongs to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: Projections, beams or ledges sticking out from a wall
To extend outward

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם רָצָה לְהוֹצִיא בָּהּ זִיזִין, מוֹצִיא.
phrases.english: That if he wants to extend projections from it, he may extend them.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller may extend projections from the upper story

steps.title: רב פפא: the seller may rebuild the upper story
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the seller may build an upper story on top if the old one falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If he wants to build an upper story on top of it, he may build.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer. The seller keeps the right to build an upper story there again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב פפא, what the seller keeps is his right to that space. Even if the upper story falls down, he may put up a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of it
He may build

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם רָצָה לִבְנוֹת עֲלִיָּיה עַל גַּבָּהּ, בּוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: That if he wants to build an upper story on top of it, he may build.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller may rebuild an upper story there

steps.title: Only רב זביד fits the words 'זאת אומרת'
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד's answer fits ריש לקיש's opening words 'זאת אומרת' ('this means'), but רב פפא's answer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רב זביד, because that is why it says 'this means.' But for רב פפא, what does 'this means' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. ריש לקיש opened with 'זאת אומרת', which shows he was learning something from an earlier source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זאת אומרת' means the rule is learned from an earlier source. רב זביד's projections can be learned that way. The right to rebuild is not learned from that source, so the words do not fit רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (one view)
This means, a phrase showing a rule is learned from an earlier source
But (introducing the problem for the other view)

phrases.english: It works for Rav Zevid,
that is why he teaches 'this means';
but for Rav Pappa,
what is the meaning of 'this means'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב זְבִיד הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's wording 'זאת אומרת' shows he was learning from a source. רב פפא's rule does not come from that source.

steps.title: רב פפא's view remains difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends this discussion by saying the problem with רב פפא stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer for רב פפא. The challenge is left standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' here means the question is unanswered. It does not mean רב פפא's rule is wrong in practice. It only means his view does not explain ריש לקיש's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד: keeping the upper story lets the seller extend projections. רב פפא: it lets him rebuild. Only רב זביד fits the words 'זאת אומרת', so רב פפא is left with a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not a full rejection like 'תיובתא'. It means the question has no answer here, but the view is not thrown out.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The problem with רב פפא stays unanswered. רב זביד's explanation fits ריש לקיש's wording.

steps.title: רב דימי: a house sale needs two phrases
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא teaches that writing 'depth and height' is not enough. The seller must also write 'from the depths of the earth to the height of the sky.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: Someone who sells a house to another person, even if he wrote for him 'depth and height,' must also write for him: 'Acquire for yourself from the depths of the earth until the height of the sky.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: which words in a sale document include which parts of the property. רב דימי says a house sale needs two separate phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think 'depth and height' already covers everything. רב דימי says a second, wider phrase is still needed. The next steps explain what each phrase adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Depth and height, the space below and above the house
Who sells
From the depths of the earth to the height of the sky
Acquire for yourself

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דִּמְזַבֵּין לֵיהּ בֵּיתָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: One who sells a house to his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתַב לֵיהּ: ״עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא״,
phrases.english: even though he wrote for him: 'depth and height,'
he must write for him:
'Acquire for yourself from the depths of the earth
until the height of the sky.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house sale document needs both 'depth and height' and 'from the depths of the earth to the height of the sky'.

steps.title: Why are both phrases needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב דימי's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the seller must write both phrases. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both phrases meant the same thing, one would be extra. The גמרא wants to know what each phrase adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.title: Each phrase covers something different
steps.stepSummary: With no special wording, the buyer does not get depth and height. 'Depth and height' gives him that space. The wider phrase gives him the pit, the cistern and the tunnels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because depth and height are not acquired with no special wording. 'Depth and height' works to acquire depth and height, and 'from the depths of the earth until the height of the sky' works to acquire a pit, a cistern and tunnels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב דימי. Each phrase gives the buyer a different part of the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain sale gives only the house itself, without the right to dig below or build above. 'Depth and height' adds that space. The wider phrase adds the בור, דות and מחילות, which a plain sale does not include.

keyTerms.meaning: With no special wording
Has an effect, does something
A dug pit and a built cistern
Tunnels, underground passages

phrases.english: Because depth and height he does not acquire with no special wording;
'depth and height' works
to acquire depth and height,
and 'from the depths of the earth until the height of the sky' works
to acquire a pit, a cistern and tunnels.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A plain sale does not include depth and height. 'Depth and height' adds that space. The wider phrase adds the pit, cistern and tunnels.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how much each phrase in a sale document matters. Every phrase is read as adding something real.

steps.title: A משנה that might support רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests support from a משנה. It says a house sale does not include the pit or the cistern, even if 'depth and height' was written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: 'And not the pit and not the cistern, even though he wrote for him depth and height'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that might support רב דימי. The reasoning behind the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה agrees with רב דימי that 'depth and height' does not give the pit and cistern. Whether this really proves his view depends on the argument that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (this source) supports him?
Even though he wrote for him

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת –
phrases.english: 'And not the pit and not the cistern,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ ״עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא״.
phrases.english: even though he wrote for him depth and height.'
phrases.notes: This line comes from the משנה later on, which lists what is not included when someone sells a house.

steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's rule that a plain sale does not include depth and height
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה saying the pit and cistern are not included even with 'depth and height'

steps.title: How the משנה would prove רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: Suppose a plain sale already included depth and height. Then writing 'depth and height' would be extra, so it should at least give the pit and cistern. Since the משנה says it does not, depth and height must not come with a plain sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that with no special wording he acquires depth and height, then let 'depth and height' work to acquire a pit, a cistern and tunnels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proof. If the words 'depth and height' added nothing new, they would have to mean something more, like the pit and cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words in a sale document are never treated as wasted. If depth and height came anyway, writing them would have to add the pit and cistern. The משנה says they do not, so the words must be giving depth and height itself, just as רב דימי said.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you think (that)
Let it work, let it have an effect

phrases.english: And if you think
that with no special wording he acquires depth and height,
let 'depth and height' work
to acquire a pit, a cistern and tunnels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ בִּסְתָמָא קָנֵי עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא
steps.raayaSupportSource: If 'depth and height' were extra, it would have to give the pit and cistern. The משנה says it does not.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: he did not write it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It says the משנה is talking about a case where those words were not written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he did not write it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof in very few words. The case in the משנה is one where these words were not written, so nothing can be learned about what they would add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the משנה's case has 'depth and height' written and still gives no pit. If the case is read as one where it was not written, the משנה tells us nothing about what the words add, and רב דימי gets no support from here.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he did not write it for him

steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי: 'depth and height' gives the space below and above, and 'from the depths of the earth to the height of the sky' gives the pit, cistern and tunnels. The משנה brought as support was pushed aside, so his rule stands on its own reasoning.

phrases.english: Where he did not write it for him.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה. רב דימי's rule itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's case is read as one where the words were not written, so it says nothing about what they would add.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'even if he wrote'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection in step 11. The משנה clearly says 'even if he wrote,' so it cannot be about a case where nothing was written.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'even though he wrote for him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own rejection from step 11. The words of the משנה say 'even if he wrote,' so the משנה must be talking about a case where the words WERE written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 tried to escape the proof by saying the משנה is about a sale where 'depth and height' was not written. But the משנה's own wording, אף על פי שכתב לו, describes a sale where it was written. So that escape seems to go against the plain text.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here... (opens a challenge from a source)
Even though he wrote for him
It teaches / the source says

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ״ קָתָנֵי!
phrases.english: But it teaches 'even though he wrote for him'!
phrases.notes: The quote is from the משנה in step 9: the pit and cistern are not sold, even if he wrote 'depth and height.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 11 using the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that the משנה is about a case where 'depth and height' was not written.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'even though he wrote,' so it plainly covers a case where the words were written.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה in two parts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means two things. Even without writing it, the buyer gets depth and height, as if it were written. But he gets the pit, cistern and tunnels only if 'depth and height' was actually written.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: even though he did not write it for him, it counts as if he wrote it, for getting the depth and height. But for getting the pit, the cistern and the tunnels: if he wrote 'depth and height' for him, the buyer gets them. If he did not write it, the buyer does not get them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the משנה really means. It splits the rule in two: depth and height come with the house anyway, but the pit and cistern need the words 'depth and height' actually written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer reads the משנה as 'even though he did NOT write.' For depth and height, a sale with no wording is treated as if the words were written. The written words still matter, because only they give the pit, cistern and tunnels. So the משנה fits the view that a plain sale includes depth and height, and the proof for רב דימי from step 10 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)
It counts as if he wrote it
For the purpose of acquiring
Underground tunnels
He acquires

steps.whatToRemember: This is how the rejection reads the משנה, not a final ruling. On this reading, depth and height come with the house even with nothing written, and the pit, cistern and tunnels come only if 'depth and height' was actually written. That differs from רב דימי, who holds a plain sale does not include depth and height. So the משנה gives him no support.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two things the buyer can get. The 'as if written' rule gives only depth and height. The pit and cistern still need the words really written.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כָּתַב לוֹ,
phrases.english: Even though he did not write it for him,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading the משנה's 'even though he wrote' as 'even though he did NOT write.'

phrases.english: it counts as if he had written it –
for acquiring the depth and the height.
For acquiring the pit, the cistern and the tunnels –
if he wrote for him 'depth and height,' he acquires them,
and if he did not write it, he does not acquire them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by rereading the משנה, so the proof from step 10 is turned away.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (הכי קאמר), splitting it into two separate rules.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'even though he wrote' seemed to describe a sale where 'depth and height' was written, which would support the proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means 'even though he did not write.' Depth and height come as if written. The pit and cistern need the words actually written.

steps.title: A new source: the roof with a ten-טפחים railing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another line from the משנה. A house sale does not include the roof when it has a railing ten טפחים high. This sets up a new test of the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And he did not sell the roof' when it has a railing ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to test the rule with a different line of the משנה. This step only brings the source. The argument built from it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a roof with a railing ten טפחים high is not part of the house sale. The גמרא will use this case about the space above the house to learn something about 'height.' For now, it is only setting up the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (brings a source as proof)
Roof
Railing / guard wall around a roof
Ten handbreadths, a standard height in הלכה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And not the roof' –
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה listing what is not sold with a house.

phrases.english: when it has a railing
ten handbreadths high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned away, the גמרא brings a new source from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether depth and height (the space above and below) come with a plain house sale.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: the roof is not sold with the house when it has a railing ten טפחים high.
